newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sees 14.8 pct rise in 1997 tobacco output.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sees 14.8 pct rise in 1997 tobacco output.

text.p: Turkey expects tobacco production to reach 224,000 tonnes in 1997, up 14.8 percent from the previous year, said an official from TEKEL, state monopoly on tobacco, wine and spirits.

State Minister Nafiz Kurt said at the launch of the harvest season in western Marmara that limitations imposed on producers in different regions were lifted as tobacco stocks were reduced to satisfactory levels.

"89,000 tonnes of tobacco worth 3.4 trillion lira were burned between the years 1994-1996 when excess output reached peak levels. But this crisis is over and tobacco stocks are at 210,000 tonnes needed for cigarette production," Kurt said.
He said tobacco exports which rose to $100 million in 1996 from $92.2 million in 1995 and $37.6 in 1994 had also helped to reduce the stocks.

The Tekel official said Turkey had imposed quotas on tobacco production in the past three years, but producers were now encouraged to aim for better quality, depending on the country's production programme.
Kurt said production of tobacco to replace types currently imported from the United States and Africa were planned in the Marmara and southeast regions.
"TEKEL is working on it by setting up a joint venture with a foreign company," Kurt said but did not elaborate.
He said Turkey's current tobacco imports stood at an average of $175 to $200 million per year to produce cigarettes from blended tobacco by using local, Virginia and Burley types.
The western Aegean region is the leading tobacco producer in Turkey, followed by the southeast, Black Sea, east and Marmara.
